SONA 2018 Ramaphosa for President

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After a tumultuous week of trying to get Zuma to step down finally Ramaphosa get to deliver his first SONA

Unique Selling Point:
One of the most dramatic weeks in South African political history unfolded this week. The President refused to resign and threatened the ruling party that they would regret it if they forced him to go as he had done nothing wrong. He finally resigned with an hour and half before the deadline holding the Nation to ransom to the last hour. Now his whole cabinet is dissolved. Parliament now elects Cyril Ramaphosa as the new president denying Julius Malema his moment of glory with the 9th Vote of No Confidence in the National Assembly. It will be the first State of the Nation address which will allow the President to proceed without major disruption from the opposition

Cyril Ramaphosa will be sworn in as the new president of South Africa on Friday morning and deliver the State of the Nation address a few hours later- never before has South Africa seen a forced removal of President and the election of a new president over night


Summary:
Since Ramaphosa’s election as ANC president in December he has already effected dramatic changes the most striking being the replacement of the board of Eskom. Wednesday saw the arrest of 5 members of the Gupta family around the Vrede Dairy farm indicates a major step forward for the Hawks and their ability to move on corruption.
Friday night will be Ramaphosa first State of the Nation Address the nation and the world are watching to see if he can take South Africa into a new era ridding the cabinet of corrupt officials and stabilizing the economy but he steps into the position leading a party deeply divided party. Can he keep the Zuma faction under control in Kwa Zulu Natal - Zuma was making veiled threats on Wednesday afternoon but his departing message was no violence in my name? Will he remove Minister of Finance Malusi Gigaba before the budget speech? Can he pull the South African economy back from brink with of collapse?

Script:


Script: A new dawn in South African politics – a new era free of corruption serving South Africa as a servant of the people – this was Cyril Ramphosa message mere 24 hours after he was elected president
Link : This has been one of the most dramatic weeks in SA politics culminating in Cyril Ramaphosa making his first state of the nation address, bringing with it some anticipation and renewed hope
Mmusi Maimne ”We have had 9 years of an abusive relationship with the president it’s time we got rid of that era and talk about the South Africa we want to build
Buthelezi “He said he wants to be the servant of the people of South Africa not just of the ANC I mean those words to me those words were very profound
Script: Parliament erupted as Chief Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng and his fellow judges entered the chamber, celebrating the role they played in lifting the dark cloud of corruption and misrule that has hung over the country this past 9 years.
Ramaphosa “We should honour Madiba by putting behind us the era of discord, the era of disunity and the era of disillusionment. That has somehow engulfed our country. We should put behind us the era of diminishing trust in public institutions and weakened confidence in our countries public leaders. We should put all the negativity that has dogged our country behind us because a new dawn is upon us.
Script: This theme of a new dawn with a different style of leadership was encouraging says political analyst Judith February
Judith February “He has been waiting for this moment for all his life and he has always been the nearly man of South African politics and think he realises this is his moment to distinguish himself and also to set himself apart
Script: Seasoned political commentator Richard Calland thought the address was politically deft
Richard Calland “ think it would provoke hope across this nation I think it was a clarion call to each and every citizen of this country and I think because of its inclusive nature, which was a real bounce back to the 1990s and the era of Nelson Mandela, it was a real one nation speech
Script: Head of the Graduate School of Business Prof Mills Soko thought it signalled a clean break with the Zuma years of corruption and scandals
Mills “It is a new dawn but must not be a false dawn – that means we have to work very hard all of us with the leadership in this country to ensure that the nightmare of the past years is reversed and we address the underlying challenges that face this country
Script: President Ramphosa addressed the issue of corruption throughout his speech
Ramaphosa”We are determined to build a society defined by decency and integrity, that does not tolerate the plunder of public resources, nor the theft by corporate criminals of the hard-earned savings of ordinary people.
Script: And then he turned on corruption within the state
Ramaphosa”This is the year in which we will turn the tide on corruption in our public institutions. 1:07:10 The criminal justice institutions have been taking initiatives that will enable us to deal effectively with corruption.
Script: Once everyone was on board it was down to the hard issues the nation had been waiting to hear
Ramaphosa ”Our most grave and most pressing challenge is youth unemployment . ..Young South Africans will be moved to the centre of our economic agenda.
Richard “It’s core message apart from job creation was the need to drive inclusive growth. The core message was of renewal and hope, and of course at a time like this, a speech should not necessarily be about the detail of policy, it’s got to tell the people of this country that we have new leadership a leadership that can be trusted
Script: The speech didn’t skirt the controversial issue of land reform
Ramaphosa “Guided by the resolutions of the 54th National Conference of the governing party, this approach will include the expropriation of land without compensation.
Lekhota “He didn’t tell us from whom is the land going to be taken and to whom is it going to be given .This uncertainty is dangerous it is going to put South African against South African
Richard “ The caveat came in the part of the speech right after that where the president – Ramaphosa, I am having to get used to saying that - where president Ramaphosa said we will expropriate without compensation but only where it drives productive use of land and only where it helps solve the problem of food insecurity
Script Free higher education - what some have called the poisoned chalice that Zuma left him, Ramaphosa handled by not changing a thing leaving it to the budget speech and the Minister of Higher Education
Ramaphosa “free higher education and training will be available to first year students from households that have gross combined annual income of up to R350,000
Mac Farlane “ What didn’t we get from this speech?
Judith I thought he might have said more about education that for example having a matric pass rate that increases is simply no marker of the kind of the standard we are maintaining but he had a very a short time to prepare this speech and so I think we have to give him the benefit of the doubt.
Script: On the issue of social grants he said he wouldn’t tolerate the current chaos
Ramaphosa “I want to personally allay fears of any disruption to the efficient delivery of this critical service, and I will take action to ensure no person in government should undermine the implementation deadlines that have been set by the court.
Richard “He made an extraordinary statement he said that he wold not allow anybody in government to get in the way of the effective delivery of those social grants and it was notable that the one cabinet minister who was absent this evening was Bathabile Dlamini
Macfarlane “How does he begin getting rid of the rot
Richard “Well his statement about the governance of the state owned enterprises was very clear it was categorical it said they have been behaving like executive committees they have been making operation decisions including the around tenders and procurement and that is where the corruption bites what he said is that must stop
Macfarlane “He has got to fire people do you think that is the first order of business
Judith “His first order of business will be to put together his cabinet because there was’nt the motion of no confidence which would have also collapsed the cabinet so he is able to then retain some individuals there will of necessity have to be some compromises because of the division within the ANC
Script: Critically, he tackled the issue of the bloated cabinet and civil service
Ramaphosa “. We will therefore initiate a process to review the configuration, the number and size of national government departments.
Lekhota “Too much of public funds is being consumed by a cabinet of 73 minister and deputy ministers. President Mandela had a government of national unity when he started here he had a cabinet of only 28
MacFarlane He made some bold statements he spoke about state owned enterprises but he also spoke about chapter 9 institutions first and foremost he needs to deal with a National Directorate of Public Prosecutions
Richard “well again he ticked all the boxes. He said that he has to make a very important appointment as the new National Directorate of Prosecutions because that person has to also renew the mandate and the effectiveness of the national prosecuting authority. He also pointed the spot light at Tom Moyane who is the head of the SARS and he appointed a commission of enquiry to find out what is going on there. Moyani won’t last long I am certain of that because Ramaphosa realises that revenue collection is such an important part of any governments business but especially when you are short of money
Script: For the first time in many years the State of the Nation address was delivered without disruptions or points of order. There was a great sense of relief and unity as the parliamentarians emerged
Mac Farlane “Are you looking forward to working with him
Steenhuisen”I think so anything is better than Mr Zuma but this is the same ANC benches that has sat and protected Mr Zuma for last 5 years
Malema “He was sworn in yesterday he tried his level best let’s give him chance we gave him chances EFF we will hold him accountable based on his commitments
Link “As you can see in the background jubilation and excitement the song that is being sung is that it’s now time for Cyril Ramaphosa it is time for Cyril Ramaphosa to stand up as you can see parliamentarians excited by the dawn of a new president and ideally the dawn of a new era for South Africa
Ramaphosa “We are at a moment in the history of our nation when the people, through their determination, have started to turn our country around. ..Now is the time when all of us should lend a hand. Now is the time for each one of us to say South Africa, ‘send me’. Now is the time for all of us to work together, this is now the time we should honour the memory of Nelson Mandela, to build a new, better South Africa for all our people now is the time. Thank you very much
